_comment: U4, transcript-based trimming. This feature is a good mutation target for the reason the
technique exists in this project: almost nothing here fails loudly. A cut list applied to
the wrong timeline still encodes. Cuts that silently replace the filler-removal plan still
produce a shorter clip that looks plausible. A dropped cut list produces the clip the user
already had, which is exactly what they will assume they are looking at until they check.
The mutations below fall into four groups: the geometry (does the plan describe the right
regions), the refusals (does a request that cannot be honoured get declined rather than
approximated), the wiring (does the cut list actually reach ffmpeg), and the reporting (does
the clip record tell the truth about what happened).

mutations.name: no_minimum_segment
mutations.why: two adjacent cuts leave a 50 ms sliver; rendered it is a frame of video and an audible click, and it still encodes without complaint

mutations.name: accept_non_finite_cuts
mutations.old:
if not (math.isfinite(lo) and math.isfinite(hi)):
        return None
mutations.why: NaN survives float() and then makes sorting undefined and every duration meaningless, all the way into an ffmpeg argument

mutations.name: cuts_replace_the_filler_plan
mutations.why: filler removal and a cut list both want regions gone; dropping the intersection makes the cut list win, silently restoring the ums

mutations.name: render_an_empty_clip
mutations.old:
if not keeps:
        return TrimPlan(keeps=fallback, cut_count=len(ordered), refusal="empty_result")
mutations.new:
if not keeps:
        return TrimPlan(keeps=[], cut_count=len(ordered), removed_seconds=span)
mutations.why: striking every word must be refused, not rendered: an empty keep list is a concat with no inputs

mutations.name: drop_the_cut_limit
mutations.old:
if len(ordered) > MAX_CUTS:
        return TrimPlan(keeps=fallback, cut_count=len(ordered), refusal="too_many_cuts")
mutations.why: the filter graph grows linearly with the cut count, so an unbounded list makes the graph the failure rather than the edit

mutations.name: refusal_reports_success
mutations.why: a declined trim reported as an applied one is the mislabelling the degradation-marker convention exists to prevent

mutations.name: refused_plan_is_still_changed
mutations.why: a refused plan must not trigger a re-encode; `keeps` then describes the clip as it already was

mutations.name: removed_measured_against_the_window
mutations.old: base_total = sum(k.duration for k in fallback) if fallback else span
mutations.why: measured against the full window rather than the post-filler timeline, a cut inside an already-removed region looks like progress and costs a second re-encode

mutations.name: no_coalescing
mutations.why: ASR word boundaries are rarely exactly adjacent, so without a gap tolerance two struck neighbours leave a rounding-width sliver between them

mutations.name: reversed_pair_dropped
mutations.old:
if hi < lo:
            lo, hi = hi, lo
mutations.why: a selection dragged right-to-left arrives reversed; dropping it loses the edit with no error

mutations.name: pipeline_ignores_the_cut_list
mutations.why: the whole feature unwired: every clip renders exactly as before and the API still returns 200

mutations.name: pipeline_loses_the_filler_plan
mutations.why: the seam between the two features: without the base plan, a cut list quietly discards filler removal's work

mutations.name: markers_not_recorded
mutations.why: an applied trim with no marker is indistinguishable from one that never ran, which is the only thing the caller can see

mutations.name: duration_reports_the_window
mutations.why: reporting the source window means a successful trim is reported as having changed nothing - the pre-U4 defect this fixed

mutations.name: refusal_marker_not_recorded
mutations.why: a refused edit with no explanation on the clip record is indistinguishable from a broken feature

mutations.name: api_drops_the_cuts
mutations.old: cuts=[(c.start, c.end) for c in req.cuts],
mutations.why: the request validates, the render succeeds, the response is 200, and the user's edit is gone

mutations.name: api_skips_the_cut_limit
mutations.why: an oversized list should be a 422 naming the limit, not a marker the caller has to go hunting for

mutations.name: trimmed_flag_by_prefix
mutations.old: trimmed = any(marker in ("filler_removal", trim_mod.MARKER) for marker in effects)
mutations.new: trimmed = any(marker.startswith(("filler_removal", trim_mod.MARKER)) for marker in effects)
mutations.why: `transcript_trim_refused:*` shares the applied marker's prefix, so a prefix test reports the clip as trimmed in exactly the case where the trim did not happen

mutations.name: rerender_drops_the_cuts
mutations.why: the one line that carries the cut list from the HTTP layer onto the candidate the pipeline reads

mutations.name: transcript_endpoint_transcribes_on_a_miss
mutations.why: a miss returned as an empty transcript tells the UI 'this clip has no words' when the truth is 'I cannot tell you this clip's words' - two things that call for opposite behaviour

mutations.name: cache_key_ignores_the_vocabulary
mutations.why: the vocabulary prompt shapes the transcript, so ignoring it in the key serves the editor words the render never produced

mutations.name: clip_relative_words_left_source_relative
mutations.why: cut offsets are clip-relative; source-relative words would have the user striking a word and losing a different one
